findings.claim: normalizer.py:1638 `metadata = json.loads(document["metadata_json"])` is UNGUARDED and OUTSIDE any try in normalize_catalog, so ONE malformed documents.metadata_json still aborts the WHOLE normalization run - the exact failure mode batch 2 says it fixed, left standing in the sibling parse three lines above.
findings.evidence: AST: the only ast.Try in normalize_catalog starts at 1664 and its body is 1665-1679; both 1638 and the _frontmatter call at 1731 are outside it. Probe %TEMP%\b10vr3\probes\p_normalize_abort.py seeds a throwaway catalog through the product's own CatalogStore with one row whose metadata_json is 'not json at all' and calls normalize_catalog: 'ESCAPED: JSONDecodeError -> Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)' raised from normalizer.py:1638, nothing recorded. Neither caller protects it: service.py:194 returns normalize_catalog(...) directly inside only a CatalogOperationLock, and cli.py:958 calls get_catalog().normalize(...).
findings.impact: On a catalog containing any document whose metadata_json is not valid JSON, `company-wiki catalog normalize` aborts on that document instead of degrading it: no ProcessingReport, no per-document failure record, no attempt counting, and every document queued BEHIND it is never normalized. This directly violates the B05 contract the evidence invokes ('malformed content must never crash the ingest path'), which is the contract batch 2 was written to satisfy.
findings.suggested_disposition: Treat the parse at 1638 exactly like _frontmatter: hand it to store.metadata_object, or move the parse+use inside a per-document guard. If the exception TYPE must keep reaching failure_reasons, ALSO move the parse inside the try at 1664 - today it cannot reach it at all. Do not close this by editing the registry text only.

findings.claim: normalizer.py::normalize_catalog is registered in EXPLICIT_NON_CHAIN_READERS on a FALSE premise, so a declared 'deliberate non-chain reader' is in fact an unguarded crash path.
findings.evidence: read_chain.py:150-156 states 'the parse at :1633 sits in normalize_catalog's per-document try, and the handler at :1689 records error_code = type(exc).__name__ into normalization_metadata_json and the report's failure_reasons ... today: JSONDecodeError for malformed, TypeError for NULL, AttributeError for a non-object payload'. My structural map shows the handler at 1688 covers only 1665-1679, so none of those three types is recorded; the malformed case (JSONDecodeError) and the NULL case (TypeError from json.loads(None)) abort the run, and the non-object payload case raises AttributeError at the `metadata.get("dayu_meta")` on line 1639 - also outside the try, so also an abort, not a record.
findings.impact: The registry is the artefact a future converger reads to decide what is safe to leave alone. Its stated reason is wrong in the direction that KEEPS the defect: a reader is excused as 'deliberate, its exception type is recorded data' when in reality nothing is recorded at all. It also makes the registry's own audit trail false, and the EXPLICIT_NON_CHAIN/CONFIRMED set equality assertion (test_b10_read_chain.py:361-367) locks the wrong entry into place.
findings.suggested_disposition: Correct the declaration to the measured truth (unguarded crash site, not a recorded-type raise) and either guard it or register it as a known OPEN defect rather than a design decision. Findings 01 and 02 have the same root: the site was declared from the failure-path docstring's reputation instead of from its control flow.

findings.claim: _frontmatter's degradation does not tell the identity layer that the metadata is missing, so a row with an UNREADABLE metadata_json now records an identity PASS ('consistent') instead of 'no evidence'.
findings.evidence: _frontmatter passes publisher=inner.get('publisher') with inner={} when metadata is unreadable, and assess_homepage_identity returns {'verdict': 'consistent'} as soon as ANY declared value appears verbatim in the first page - in that call the only declared value left is the document title, which trivially appears. Measured: assess_homepage_identity('Test Filing\nbody text', title='Test Filing', publisher=None) -> {'verdict': 'consistent', 'evidence': {'declared_count': 1}} and homepage_identity_quality_flag('consistent') -> None (no quality flag). Meanwhile detect_entities with declared_entity=None returns 'unverifiable', which also raises no flag. Net effect on the degraded path: zero quality flags, identity='consistent', declared entity and security ids simply absent from the rendered frontmatter (the shipped tolerance test asserts exactly that absence).
findings.impact: Opting out of the entity/publisher declaration silently converts an uncheckable identity into a recorded PASS. The old code did not have this hole because it raised - but that fix must not buy tolerance at the price of a false pass: the convergence removes the crash AND removes the signal, so the row looks cleaner than a row that was never declarable in the first place. This is the 'evidence missing recorded as passed' failure mode, arrived at from the opposite direction.
findings.suggested_disposition: Thread the metadata state into _frontmatter (it is already available as metadata_state(...)[1]) and record 'unverifiable: metadata unreadable' - or add a quality flag such as metadata_unreadable - so degradation is visible in the artifact rather than invisible.

findings.claim: The registry's line-number citations were left at the pre-batch-1 revision.
findings.evidence: EXPLICIT_NON_CHAIN_READERS says ':1633' and ':1689'; at d92bb33 those were exactly right (metadata = json.loads(...) at 1633, error_code at 1689) but at 5ec18a5 the same statements are at 1638 and 1694. read_chain.py:1400's '1739' is also stale. read_chain.py:139-140's 'normalizer.py:1726' is right for d92bb33 and off by five for the tree it ships with (1731).
findings.impact: The citations resolve to the right statements, so this is not misleading about content - but a registry whose whole point is to be the machine-checkable statement of the read chain should not cite line numbers that no longer exist. A future reader who greps 1633 lands on a progress() call.
findings.suggested_disposition: Re-anchor the citations (or cite symbols instead of line numbers) in the same change that fixes -01/-02.

findings.claim: The 'exception TYPE is recorded data' argument for leaving normalize_catalog unconverted does not survive contact with the rest of the codebase, even setting aside that it never reaches failure_reasons.
findings.evidence: The handler's own fallback is `DOCUMENT_PARSE_TIMEOUT_CODE if isinstance(exc, NormalizationTimeoutError) else type(exc).__name__` (normalizer.py:1694-1698), i.e. the codebase already folds a large family of parser exceptions into a type-name-derived code, and normalization_metadata_json/error_code are diagnostic fields, not a frozen contract constant.
findings.impact: Small: it means the one justification offered for keeping this site unconverged is weaker than the registry implies, which matters because the same justification is what makes the site look settled.
findings.suggested_disposition: If the owner does want the type preserved, say so as a decision with the alternative named; do not rest it on 'it is recorded data' alone.

findings.claim: The two ratchets' scope boundary is true but load-bearing: they can only see src/company_wiki/source_catalog.
findings.evidence: The contract test scans SOURCE = tests/../src/company_wiki/source_catalog recursively. Real direct readers of the same columns live outside it: scripts/legacy_observer.py:96, scripts/wu904_remediation_restore.py:65, and eleven contract tests including tests/contract/test_r4b05_metadata_provenance.py:136 and tests/contract/test_source_catalog_section_extractor.py:168.
findings.impact: Low and NOT introduced by this batch - those sites predate B10 and the gate's reach is explicitly documented in GATE_BOUNDARIES, which is better than the usual case. Recorded because EXPLICIT_NON_CHAIN_READERS reads as though the read chain were enumerated for the repository, while it is enumerated for one package.
findings.suggested_disposition: Add one boundary entry naming the out-of-package readers so the next reader of the registry does not mistake the package scope for the repository scope.

findings.claim: The evidence document carries two generations of numbers and section 7bis was not updated.
findings.evidence: b10-implementation.md section 7bis states 'gate 13 cases' and 'mutation 8/8 KILLED'; section 7quater states 'gate 14 cases' and 'mutation 9/9'. The tree and the evidence JSON agree with 7quater (14 collected, 9 mutants). Section 7ter also says CONFIRMED_DIRECT_READERS 'only 3 left (normalizer x2 + section_query)' while the shipped registry has 2 - 7quater's own text ('x2') is the correct one.

adjudication_reason: The two repairs this round is built on are REAL and I reproduced both, so the ratchet's counting fix and the harness's syntax-kill fix are accepted without reservation: four independent probes (second reader in a baselined scope, second handoff in the 13-scope ratchet, reader in a new module, site removed without lowering the count) all came back RED with the intended messages, every mutated file was proved parseable first, and my own scanner reproduced the baseline to the digit (2/2 confirmed, 13 scopes / 16 handoff sites, zero mismatches). The harness re-run gave 9/9 killed_by=assertion with the repository untouched, and when I put the 8-space variant back it recorded invalid_mutant_syntax, set all_killed=false and exited 1 - exactly the guarantee claimed. The recorded evidence matches my independent run mutant for mutant, and every number in section 7quater (14 cases, 9/9, 793, 1903/8, 16 sites, both repairs) checks out against the tree and the CI logs. I found no inflation. I nevertheless REJECT, on one P0 that the batch's own reasoning should have caught: normalizer.py:1638 still parses the shared column with a bare json.loads OUTSIDE every try in normalize_catalog, and I drove a throwaway catalog through normalize_catalog to watch a single malformed metadata_json raise JSONDecodeError straight out of the whole run. That is the same abort-the-whole-normalization failure the batch-2 commit message describes at length for _frontmatter five lines below - the fix went to the sibling that was noticed and not to the one beside it. It is coupled to a P1 that makes it worse rather than better: read_chain.py declares that very site as a deliberate non-chain reader whose 'exception TYPE is recorded data', and its cited handler covers only lines 1665-1679, so the registry's justification is refuted by the control flow it describes. A third P1 records that the _frontmatter degradation now lets a row with unreadable metadata reach an identity verdict of 'consistent' with no quality flag at all - tolerance bought by removing the signal. None of the three is a large code change; -01 is a one-line convergence, -02 is a correction of a declaration, -03 is threading a state that is already computed. But B10's entire subject is that malformed data must be a recorded state rather than a crash or a silence, so shipping the convergence with an unguarded parse of the same column in the same function, and a registry entry that certifies it as intentional, is the one thing this review cannot sign.
not_checked: The production catalog was never opened, so I do not know how many real rows carry a malformed documents.metadata_json; finding -01's blast radius is therefore demonstrated on a synthetic catalog, not measured against production data.

I did not run the full unit/contract suites myself (793 / 1903+8). I verified the recorded CI tails match their claims and re-ran only the B10 gate and its unit tests; the rest is taken from evidence I read but did not reproduce.
Remote CI status was not verified (no network). The claims about e36b984 and 144345b being green on the remotes are unchecked.

batch 1's other five convergences (artifact_backfill._classify, artifact_read_model._artifact_row, scanner._previous_provenance_fields, source_lifecycle._safety_receipt, service.query_filing_candidates) were checked only structurally - registry vs scanner vs the call sites they name - and not driven input-by-input the way _frontmatter was.

I did not attempt to defeat the two ratchets in the shapes GATE_BOUNDARIES already admits are open (intermediate variable, subscript inside the callee, third-party parser). I confirmed the boundaries are documented and pinned by a test, but I did not re-probe the two that are marked PROBED.
The out-of-package readers listed in -06 were found by grep of column name + loads; I did not classify each one as a true reader or a false positive.
Tests in the two unit files were run but not adversarially mutated beyond what the shipped harness does (M9 covers the _frontmatter tolerance test).

No judgement is offered on B10 as a whole, on B10-5 (revertible version / removal conditions) or on whether the remaining sites should be converged; this review is scoped to batch 1 + batch 2 and the two repairs.
